analysis.title: One cannot live on T-bills alone - 2027 Treasury supply outlook
key_insights: JPM forecasts the federal budget deficit at $2.06tn in FY27, up from $1.992tn in FY26. At 6.1% of GDP it edges lower as a share of the economy.
The FY27 deficit forecast assumes tariff receipts recover. JPM expects Section 301 and 232 actions to lift the average effective tariff rate toward 13.8% in FY27, from 11.2% currently.
Under unchanged coupon auction sizes, JPM estimates a cumulative Treasury funding gap of about $1.6tn over FY27-28. It does not think Treasury can rely only on T-bills as it has in recent years.
The T-bill share of marketable debt is just under 23%, up from about 15% at YE22. JPM expects it to rise above 24% by YE27 even with coupon increases starting later next year.

T-bills now trade cheap to SOFR for the first time since late 2022, while 2-year notes have richened on an asset swap basis YTD. JPM reads this as early signs that T-bill demand is becoming inelastic.
JPM expects money-fund AUM growth to slow toward the mid-single-digit range. Foreign official holdings have given less support, and stablecoin AUM has been flat for 18 months.

JPM expects a multi-quarter series of nominal coupon auction size increases starting at the August 2027 refunding, concentrated in 2s through 10s, TIPS and FRNs. It expects an increase to the October new-issue 5-year TIPS.

Treasury removed 'at least' from its forward guidance at the November refunding and now 'anticipates maintaining nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for the next several quarters'. JPM reads this as more flexibility to raise sizes later in FY27.
The November TBAC minutes show broad agreement to increase coupon sizes, with considerable debate over the pace and sizing at the long end.

JPM expects 20- and 30-year auction sizes to stay unchanged through 2027. It cites solid primary demand and healthy long-end market functioning, and sees the November refunding as lowering the probability of long-end cuts.
Gross coupon, TIPS and FRN issuance is forecast at $4.511tn in 2027, $116bn above 2026's $4.395tn. The largest increases are $30bn each in 2s and 5s.
JPM forecasts $2.226tn of net privately-held borrowing in 2027, versus $2.181tn in 2026. That includes $1.011tn of bills and $1.036tn of coupons.

JPM expects the Fed to absorb about $180bn of bill supply in 2027 through MBS paydown reinvestment of about $15bn a month, versus $360bn in 2026. Risks are skewed lower in 2H27 if Chair Warsh's balance sheet task force ends the reinvestment.

The debt ceiling should bind around February, with Treasury about $694bn below the limit as of November 12. Extraordinary measures and a large TGA balance should produce negative net T-bill issuance through at least 2Q27.
JPM projects the WAM of marketable Treasury debt falling from about 69 months to 68 months by YE27 and 67 months by YE28.

Risks: weaker tariff receipts or a wider deficit could pull coupon increases forward, while a smaller borrowing need would let Treasury lean on bills longer. A cut to long-end auction sizes remains a political risk given Secretary Bessent's focus on lowering long-term rates.
JPM sees a growing likelihood of a 1-year SOFR-indexed FRN being introduced in 2027. The November TBAC minutes say the Committee agreed that exploring it would be worthwhile.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The deficit widened $217bn in FY26 even as nominal GDP growth exceeded 5.5%. Outlays rose 6% against receipts up 3%, partly reflecting tariff repayments after the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs.
A wider deficit raises Treasury's financing needs and supports coupon auction size increases.
The Figure 1 chart data shows a further widening in FY28.
The starting point for JPM's tariff receipts recovery assumption.
The forecast depends on Section 301 and 232 actions. Further legal challenges and the new Democratic Congress could constrain it.
Rising bill share and price-sensitive marginal demand are the case for Treasury to increase coupon sizes.
Starting point for the projected decline.

macro_indicators.reading: 68 months by YE27, 67 months by YE28
macro_indicators.interpretation: Heavier bill and short-coupon issuance shortens the average maturity.

macro_indicators.indicator: Treasury headroom under the statutory debt limit
macro_indicators.interpretation: JPM expects the debt ceiling to bind around February, after which extraordinary measures keep net bill issuance negative through at least 2Q27.

crypto_views: Stablecoin AUM has been stagnant for the last 18 months, which JPM lists among the reasons T-bill demand is moderating.
risk_factors: Weaker tariff receipts or a wider deficit could pull coupon increases forward or require a more aggressive series of increases.
Further legal challenges and the new Democratic Congress could limit the administration's ability to raise tariffs under alternative statutory authorities.
Treasury could cut 20- and 30-year auction sizes, a political risk given Bessent's focus on lowering long-term rates.
Treasury could introduce new products such as a 1-year SOFR FRN, which would shift the composition of bill and FRN supply.
The Fed purchase forecast is skewed lower in 2H27 if Chair Warsh's balance sheet task force ends MBS reinvestment into bills.
vol_and_positioning: T-bills trade cheap to SOFR for the first time since late 2022. The 3-month T-bill matched-maturity SOFR asset swap spread is plotted in Figure 4.
2-year notes have richened on an asset swap basis YTD, in contrast to bills.

Supreme Court strike down of IEEPA tariffs earlier in 2026, with tariff repayments

tension_points.bull_case: Treasury could cut 20- and 30-year auction sizes. Secretary Bessent has called himself the 'nation's top bond salesman' and has made lowering long-term rates his main goal.
tension_points.bear_case: JPM sees little rationale to cut an existing source of borrowing capacity while financing needs rise. Long-end primary demand has been solid and market functioning has held up, and the November refunding reduced the probability of cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Treasury announcing cuts to 20- and 30-year auction sizes at a future refunding, or TBAC concluding in favor of reducing long-end issuance.

theme_stances.key_argument: With the bill share approaching 25% and marginal demand becoming more price sensitive, it is prudent for Treasury to begin increasing longer-term auction sizes in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: we think it’s prudent Treasury begin to increase longer-term auction sizes in 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: Treasury has little reason to cut 20- and 30-year auction sizes when financing needs are rising and long-end demand and functioning are healthy.
theme_stances.evidence: we see little rationale for Treasury to reduce an existing source of borrowing capacity
